newsitem.title: USA: FUND VIEW - New England High Income whittles down.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - New England High Income whittles down.

text.p: As soon as Gary Goodenough took the helm last July as co-manager of the New England High Income Fund, he began hacking away at the portfolio of nearly 140 securities.
The fund was too diverse, and its performance had suffered from the multitude of bets, he said.
"After studying the portfolio, we didn't like the structure, and didn't want to own some of those companies on a credit outlook basis, and based on their illiquidity," Goodenough said.
"Also, some of the bonds might have been callable in six months," he said. "We wanted more call protection."
Today, under Goodenough and co-manager Madeline Glick -- who both work for sub-adviser Loomis Sayles & Co -- the $67 million fund has only 37 issues, all high-yield corporate fixed income securities.
Goodenough prefers fewer issues "that we know very, very well...so we can see trouble coming before it hits."
The fund has about 7.5 percent in cash, up from about one percent at the end of the 1996.
Goodenough said the change reflects his expectation that the Federal Reserve will likely raise short-term interest rates at least once more this year.

The fund's strategy is straightforward. "Our mandate is very high coupon income," Goodenough said. "We're positioned at the top of the current yield category and the overall high yield universe. Our second missions is total return, and low volatility."
Value Line, in a report earlier this month, said, "The fund has shown strong promise under the direction of Goodenough and Glick..."
Goodenough said the average credit quality is single B, with the portfolio running from double B through triple C.
The fund must have at least 80 percent of total assets in U.S. companies, either preferred stock or convertible issues.
Up to 20 percent may be invested in common stocks and up to ten percent in fixed income securities issued by foreign governments or by companies organized in foreign governments.

Top current holdings include Grupo Televisa, zero/13-1/4 percent and due 2008, and comprising about 3.68 percent of the portfolio; Penn Traffic Co, 9-5/8 due 2005; private AMF Group, zero/12-1/4 due 2006, 3.51 percent.
Other big holdings were; Transtexas Gas Corp, 11-1/2 due 2002, at 3.38 percent; and private Big V Supermarkets Inc, 11 due 2004, at 3.34 percent.
Goodenough said any industry weighting is incidental; the approach is strictly bottom up.
According to Morningstar Inc, from July 1, 1996 through April 11, the fund has returned 10.4 percent versus an average return of 8.22 percent for the high-yield bond fund sector.
For the 12 months ended June 30, 1996, the fund 9.16 percent, versus an average of 11.41 percent.
The New England Funds is a unit of New England Investment Cos LP.
